researcher_notes: 5 files: 4 official 'Specifications' PDFs (MiR1200 Pallet Jack, MiR1350, MiR250, MiR600 -- long-form, ~10-13pp each, extremely detailed) plus a 2pp marketing 1-pager for the MiR1200 Pallet Jack that largely duplicates the specs sheet with a couple of minor figure discrepancies (see MiR1200 notes). All 4 base models already exist in the DB with every field NULL ('last_updated: unknown') -- pure enrichment, no new products, no variant completion. Extracted text has NO SPACES between words throughout all 4 long spec PDFs (a font/kerning extraction quirk, not an OCR error) but remained reliably parseable since every value is still unambiguously delimited by units/numbers. MiR250, MiR600 and MiR1350 spec sheets each contain many pages of 'operational corridor width' / 'space requirement' figures for various docking/turning/pivoting scenarios (e.g. 'Operational corridor width for a 90° turn') -- these are NOT the same quantity as AP0's min_turning_radius (they describe required surrounding clearance space, not the vehicle's own turning geometry) and were deliberately NOT mapped to any AP0 field to avoid a unit/definition mismatch.

products.notes: Marker-based docking (VL-marker/V-marker/L-marker/bar-marker) positioning-accuracy tables present (pp.2-3) but this document never states the robot's PRIMARY navigation technology (no 'SLAM' or 'natural feature' keyword found anywhere in the text) -- navigation_type deliberately left null rather than inferred from MiR's general reputation as a SLAM-based AMR vendor, per the no-external-knowledge rule. Many pages (3-8) of operational-corridor/space-requirement figures for docking, turning, pivoting and two-robots-passing scenarios intentionally not mapped to any field (see researcher_notes).
